# dataexcept: structured, classed failures that cross language boundaries

<small>Source: [`R/dataexcept-package.R`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/r-dataexcept/blob/main/R/dataexcept-package.R) · Help: `?dataexcept-package`</small>

dataexcept gives data and modelling code three things base R conditions do
not have on their own:

## Details

- **A shared vocabulary of classed errors** with structured fields -- [`missing_column_error()`](data_frame_errors.md), [`convergence_error()`](modelling_errors.md), [`api_error()`](service_errors.md) and the rest (see [`dataexcept_classes()`](dataexcept_classes.md)) -- each carrying failure metadata that says whether a retry can succeed ([`failure_metadata()`](failure_metadata.md)).
- **One failure format across R and Python.** [`condition_to_json()`](condition_to_envelope.md) writes any R condition as the envelope the Python DataExcept package publishes as a JSON Schema, and [`envelope_to_condition()`](envelope_to_condition.md) reads an envelope from either language back into an R condition that ordinary handlers catch.
- **Classes for base R's text-only warnings.** [`with_classed_warnings()`](with_classed_warnings.md) turns warnings such as `glm.fit`'s non-convergence into classed warnings, recognised in any session language.

Credentials in URLs are removed before they reach a condition or an
envelope ([`redact_url()`](redact_url.md)).
